r1 /// ... among the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) that cause cessation of existence, there is nothing to be abandoned; there is nothing permanent or impermanent to be understood — the darkness by which [the world] is cast ... with rays ... the dust of which is destroyed
2 /// ... by whom the supreme, immortal, hard-to-obtain truth has been attained; my mind and intellect take delight in him who is supreme in tranquility — Steadfastness — There is, there is that radiance called 'person' (<s>puruṣasaṃjñaka</s>), grasped by my power, that has manifested —
3 /// ... this pair [of qualities] depends upon each other. Where intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) abides, there steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>) finds its place; and where steadfastness is established, there intellect expands — Fame — Being so, you two having come
4 /// ... now ... — Intellect — So be it. And moreover — He who never has intellect is as if always asleep; he who is devoid of steadfastness is as if always intoxicated; ... and he whose fame does not
v1 (exist) /// ... whose fame endures — Fame — But where now does that <s>dharma</s> embodied as a man dwell at present? — Intellect — With powers under his own control, where indeed does he not dwell? ... like a bird in the sky, he goes, he travels
2 /// ... unattached, he enters the earth like water, he divides his form in many ways, he rains streams of water in the sky, and blazes simultaneously like a twilight cloud; at will on the mountain ... he goes and practices the <s>dharma</s> according to rule
3 /// ... [is within his] range — Steadfastness — Then let us all indeed make him our wishing-tree. For this great sage is now in the grove of the city of <s>Magadha</s> — with curled eyebrows, with hands and feet of soft, delicate webbing
4 /// ... self-controlled, he dwells without desire, his purpose fulfilled, complete in knowledge and the taste of tranquility — Then enters [the stage], radiant with a halo of light ... of supreme ... appearance, the blessed <s>Śarmā</s> ...
